facts.claim: The LLaDA paper (2025), on an 8-billion-parameter masked diffusion language model, reports that low-confidence remasking (keeping the surest guesses) consistently outperforms random remasking.
LLaDA sets the reply’s length before sampling starts: it begins from a fully masked sequence of that length, and drops whatever comes after the end-of-text token.
MDLM (2024) found simple masked diffusion works better than previously thought, approaching left-to-right models’ perplexity, and can be sampled block by block for text of any length.
SEDD (2023) reports a discrete diffusion language model competitive with GPT-2 at comparable size, and similar quality with 32× fewer network evaluations.
Fast-dLLM (2025) decodes only the tokens above a confidence threshold in parallel and adds an approximate key-value cache, reporting up to 27.6× more throughput with minimal accuracy loss.
Google DeepMind announced Gemini Diffusion on 20 May 2025 as an experimental research model that turns random noise into text, faster than its fastest model so far.
Inception, the vendor, claims its diffusion model Mercury 2 writes 1,009 tokens a second on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. The vendor’s own figure, from its blog.
